source_acquisition.search_note: The automated source-inventory row records repository_without_visual_source, but direct read-only gh inspection of the author-linked repository found five rendered PNG assets that exactly match Figures 1, 3, 7 and Tables 2–3. Its 68-entry main tree has no paper TeX/TikZ/PGF, plotting scripts, table generators, notebooks, style files, or raw figure data for the remaining objects. No local corpus/visual_sources/iclr-2026-cdc551019493/ directory exists. Therefore the source is partial_visual_source rather than an exact complete generator; the PDF remains the object-list and layout fact source.

paper_style.palette_strategy: The paper uses a saturated categorical palette for method/variant identities, red emphasis for UniImb/best values, blue underlining or fill for runners-up, and pastel severity fills in construction tables. Colors are often reinforced by direct labels, hatches, marker shapes, or row placement, but the overall system is not grayscale-safe.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: PDF captions, body text, table rules, and many table glyphs are vector PDF objects; the architecture and plotted panels are embedded raster/composite assets or rasterized chart objects. The 200 dpi render and pdfimages inspection therefore support a mixed vector/raster assessment.
paper_style.style_consistency: Table headers, mean±std notation, red-best/blue-runner conventions, and dataset order are consistent across main and appendix tables. Figure families reuse red/blue sensitivity and colored ablation bars, but architecture diagrams, polar charts, 3-D surfaces, and qualitative embeddings use different typography and visual idioms; appendix density is substantially higher than the main text.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: The overall architecture of UniImb which enhances graph representations by extracting prototypical features in an uniform manner.

color.semantic_mapping: Yellow/orange frames mark inputs and selected prototypes; green marks graph perturbation; purple/blue and red identify topology/prototype stages; black arrows and labels carry the process semantics.

encodings.x: Stage order from input graphs to prototype balancing; no quantitative x-axis
encodings.y: Parallel processing lanes and module hierarchy; no quantitative y-axis
encodings.color: Colored dashed frames assign module roles and colored graph nodes indicate head/tail or selected structures
encodings.shape: Graph nodes, prototype icons, numbered circles, arrows, and TopK selection marks
encodings.line: Large arrows establish the forward pipeline; dashed boxes and lower-lane arrows distinguish subroutines
encodings.facet: Upper representation-learning path versus lower prototype-attention/load-balance path
encodings.text: Input Graphs, Local/Global Topology Encoding, Graph Perturbation Strategy, GNN, Embedding, Dynamic Balanced Prototype, Salient Attention, Similarity, Mixing Graphs, Load Balance Optimization

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual mechanism diagram; it contains no measured samples, replicate count, estimator, or uncertainty. The lower toy matrices and activation-count example illustrate the algorithmic operations rather than data observations.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 4 uses Figure 1 as the interface for the paper’s unified claim: topology-aware augmentation feeds a prototype mechanism whose activation is balanced. Tables 1–3 quantify the prior and imbalance gains, while Figures 4–6 isolate components and representations.
design_strengths: The upper/lower lanes expose both the end-to-end path and the two-stage DBP internals.
Arrows, module frames, matrix motifs, and direct labels make the intended computation recoverable without a legend.
The page-width placement gives the method a stable visual anchor before the numerical comparisons.
design_weaknesses: Many decorative icons, mascots, equations, and labels compete for attention in the lower lane.
The repeated saturated colors and mixed typography are not robust in grayscale or at small screen sizes.
The toy activation counts are illustrative and are not explicitly separated from the empirical evidence in the caption.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a two-lane architecture: a concise end-to-end path above and a zoomed mechanism path below, with arrows and direct labels defining the interface before results.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Model performance and efficiency comparison on AirGraph dataset.

color.semantic_mapping: Bubble hue identifies method, bubble area encodes memory usage, and direct method labels identify each point; red highlights UniImb.

encodings.x: Training Speed (s/epoch), categorical method positions shown on a linear numeric scale
encodings.color: Bubble hue identifies method; red marks UniImb and a neutral bubble key identifies memory-size levels
encodings.shape: Bubble size encodes Memory-Usage; no point marker family beyond circles
encodings.line: No connecting lines; point position is the comparison grammar
encodings.text: Training Speed (s/epoch), Macro-F1, Memory-Usage, method names

figures.data_and_statistics: One point per method with Macro-F1, training time, and memory usage; no uncertainty bars or replicate ranges are shown. The surrounding setup describes AirGraph as 30,660 graphs and naturally imbalanced, but the plot itself reports only the efficiency/performance coordinates.
figures.evidence_relation: The plot operationalizes the scalability claim in Section 5.3: it places predictive performance and computational cost in one view. Table 4 supplies backbone performance and Figure 7 supplies the AirGraph distribution context.
design_strengths: Direct labels remove a lookup step for the small method set.
Bubble-size key makes memory a third quantitative dimension without a second axis.
The upper-left UniImb point communicates the claimed performance/efficiency trade-off quickly.
design_weaknesses: Bubble area and color are both visually salient, but the bubble-size key is small and overlaps the plotting field.
No error bars or exact values make close efficiency comparisons hard to audit.
Method labels and bubbles crowd the lower-left region, reducing readability at single-column width.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a labeled performance–cost bubble plot when one scalar quality metric and two resource dimensions are central; provide a separate size key and avoid relying on hue alone.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Macro-F1 (left) and Micro-F1 (right) on intertwined imbalance datasets.

color.semantic_mapping: Each method owns one radial bar color; UniImb/Ours is the dark purple series and method names are repeated in the central legend.

encodings.x: Dataset spokes arranged categorically around a polar coordinate system
encodings.y: F1 magnitude along the radial linear scale
encodings.color: Method identity is assigned to eight categorical colors, with dark purple for UniImb (Ours)
encodings.shape: Radial bar segments and central legend swatches
encodings.line: Bars extend radially from each dataset spoke; no connecting trend line
encodings.text: PROTEINS, D&D, NCI1, REDDIT-B, COLLAB, IMDB-MULTI, method legend, printed values

figures.data_and_statistics: Six datasets × eight methods are shown separately for Macro-F1 and Micro-F1. Values are point estimates; the figure does not show standard deviations, significance marks, or a replicate count.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 5.4 uses this view to compare the intertwined class/topology setting, complementing Figure 2’s AirGraph efficiency view. It supports the claim that UniImb is strongest across datasets while preserving the distinction between macro and micro metrics.
design_strengths: The two panels keep the metric distinction visible while using the same dataset spoke order.
Direct numeric labels on bars preserve exact-looking values despite the polar layout.
The central legend and repeated method palette support cross-panel comparison.
design_weaknesses: Eight colors and many printed values make the spokes dense, especially for lower-performing methods.
Polar bar lengths are harder to compare across non-adjacent spokes than aligned Cartesian bars.
No uncertainty or significance encoding is available, so apparent small gaps should not be overread.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use paired polar summaries for a compact multi-dataset overview only when direct value labels and a fixed spoke order accompany the color key; retain Cartesian tables for precise ranking.

figures.evidence_relation: This is the main component-level evidence in Section 5.5. Its variant labels map directly to the five removals described in prose; Appendix Figures 8–10 repeat the ablation family for Micro-F1 and perturbation choices.
design_strengths: The upper/lower split makes the two imbalance regimes immediately comparable.
Printed values and hatch/color redundancy reduce lookup cost.
The same dataset order is reused across both bands, allowing within-dataset component comparisons.
design_weaknesses: Six bars per group are narrow at single-column width and the legend is visually dense.
Independent y ranges/bands can make absolute changes look larger or smaller than they are.
Without uncertainty marks, the plot cannot show whether close ablation gaps exceed run variation.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use stacked regime bands with identical x categories for an ablation, and combine variant color with hatch plus direct values when bar groups are dense.

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Figure 7: Distribution of Pollution Levels in the AirGraph Dataset: High (6.86%), Medium (42.84%), and Low (50.30%).

color.semantic_mapping: Cyan, orange, and pink identify low, medium, and high pollution; pie labels carry the exact shares.

encodings.y: Relative percentage per day (%) on a linear scale; pie has no y-axis
encodings.line: Three time-series lines; no connecting grammar in pie

figures.data_and_statistics: AirGraph hourly PM2.5-derived graph instances are summarized over 2021–2023 in the text; the plotted line covers 2021–2024 labels and the pie reports the exact shares 50.30%, 42.84%, and 6.86%. No uncertainty is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix G.1.2 establishes the dataset’s natural imbalance before the main AirGraph performance/efficiency plot in Figure 2. The exact author asset in `figs/AirGraph.png` matches this PDF object, while the caption states the class-share finding directly.
design_strengths: The time-series and aggregate pie answer complementary distribution questions.
Direct percentage labels make the rare high-pollution class visible without estimating angles.
This is an exact rendered asset recovered from the author repository, preserving the source palette and labels.
design_weaknesses: The line is highly jagged and dense, so daily variation dominates long-run seasonal structure.
The pie’s exploded slice and large direct labels consume space relative to the small category.
The text says data collection through 2023 while the x-axis label reaches 2024; the visual should be read as rendered, not as a new data claim.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a temporal prevalence plot with a labeled aggregate composition view, and put the rare-class percentage in the caption rather than relying on slice area.

color.semantic_mapping: Point/graph colors identify the two class labels or highlighted prototype substructure; panel labels and node-link structure remain the primary key.

figures.data_and_statistics: Three minority-class graphs are selected by high affinity to one anchor prototype; the fourth panel highlights a common local topology. No quantitative graph-size, retrieval score, or uncertainty is printed.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix I.9 provides the strongest qualitative interpretation of DBP: prototype-to-graph affinity retrieves minority examples that share a discriminative local structure. Table 24’s DBP-only gains are the quantitative companion.
design_strengths: Matched panel labels make the retrieval-to-common-substructure argument easy to follow.
Node-link structure and highlight color directly encode the proposed prototype effect.
The montage stays qualitative and avoids implying a numeric embedding distance.
design_weaknesses: No node/edge counts or retrieval threshold are given, so the examples are not a prevalence estimate.
The network layouts are not aligned, making cross-panel geometry comparisons unsafe.
Orange/blue contrast is essential and may degrade in grayscale or for some color-vision conditions.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a retrieved-example montage followed by an explicitly highlighted shared structure to explain what a learned prototype may capture; report the retrieval rule beside it.

design_strengths: The paired rows give a direct module-addition comparison.
Only two datasets and four metrics keep the mechanism table compact.
The red DBP row cue is consistent with Tables 22–23.
design_weaknesses: “Only DBP” still leaves unspecified which training/augmentation components are held fixed.
Single-column text is small and color is not grayscale robust.
No delta column or paired test makes the size of the module gain less immediate.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a small paired addition table to isolate one module, and state the held-fixed pipeline explicitly so the result is a true module ablation.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: The visual narrative proceeds from the full UniImb mechanism (Figure 1) to prior selection and benchmark comparisons (Tables 1–3), then to efficiency, intertwined imbalance, ablation, sensitivity, transfer, and qualitative representation evidence (Figures 2–6 and Table 4–5). Appendix objects expand distribution/data construction, severity tiers, backbone coverage, hyperparameters, parameter interactions, and prototype interpretation.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use a short object title followed by setup or comparison context. Long benchmark captions define mean±std, run count, and significance only for selected tables; most chart captions identify panels but leave uncertainty, scales, and direct-label semantics to the body or visual itself. Several captions retain typographic/grammar defects such as “in an uniform,” “of on,” and “wiht.”
cross_object_system.table_header_system: The dominant table grammar is grouped dataset headers with paired Macro-F1/Micro-F1 subcolumns, plus a left method/backbone column. Construction tables switch to nested count/size/ratio headers; hyperparameter tables use one flat parameter header. This change is semantically appropriate but requires careful caption/header reading.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1’s topology encoding, perturbation, GNN, DBP, and load-balance lanes map to the named ablations in Figure 4 and Figures 8–10, while Figures 5 and 11–14 vary K/TopK settings introduced in the same diagram. Tables 22–24 then isolate backbone and DBP additions.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–6 carry the claim spine; Appendix Tables 6–24 and Figures 7–16 provide prior replication, data/split definitions, severity tiers, hyperparameters, full backbone matrices, and qualitative mechanism checks. Exact author assets are available for only five objects, so PDF-rendered observations remain authoritative for the rest.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: The surrounding PDF uses Times/Nimbus Roman and Computer Modern math for text/table material, while raster diagrams contain mixed display fonts including sans and playful display faces. Table typography is more consistent than figure-internal typography; small labels and captions are frequently near the lower readable limit.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Red marks the proposed/best result and blue marks runner-up or the second metric family in several figures, while method palettes vary by chart family. Sensitivity figures consistently use red Macro-F1 and blue Micro-F1; ablations consistently use colored/hatch bars. Cross-family semantic reuse is partial rather than global.

most_reusable_patterns: A two-lane architecture that separates the end-to-end method path from a zoomed mechanism path.
Grouped benchmark headers with paired metrics and explicit best/runner-up styling.
Regime-by-dataset small multiples for ablation and hyperparameter sensitivity, with repeated metric encodings.
Dataset-by-severity construction tables that put counts and imbalance ratios beside the split definition.
Paired baseline/+module rows for backbone applicability and DBP-only isolation.
failure_patterns: Dense single-column charts/tables rely on small text, repeated legends, and local scales.
Color and red/blue highlighting carry ranking semantics without complete grayscale redundancy.
Undefined bands and omitted per-panel sample counts limit statistical interpretation of sensitivity/qualitative plots.
Polar and perspective charts summarize well but make exact cross-method comparisons harder than the paired tables.
Caption grammar/typographic defects and occasional metric-header inconsistency reduce polish.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: UniImb uses a colorful mechanism-to-benchmark visual system: explain the unified topology/perturbation/DBP pipeline first, prove gains with wide paired-metric tables, then use regime-specific ablations, sensitivity panels, and appendix protocol tables to close the reproducibility loop.
